input.quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and indemnification (Section 8) sits outside it, but the cap base is only amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" in the preceding 12 months — a per-transaction slice that can fall far below 6 months' fees — and the only carve-out is indemnification, with nothing for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. That fails the fallback on both material terms, so we reset the base to 12 months' fees paid or payable and add the standard carve-out sentence.

input.quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Commerce One gives a defence-and-indemnity for third-party IP infringement covering us and our Customers, with the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure, procure-modify-refund remedies and only standard exclusions (out-of-documentation use, third-party modification), and it sits outside the liability cap; we owe no reciprocal indemnity. This meets the fallback (and beyond, being uncapped); it does not extend to breach of law, data breach or gross negligence, which we note but do not flag.
